I can look into this and figure out whether your Gold savings APY/interest was calculated correctly — but to access your accounts and run the checks I need to verify your identity first.

What I can tell you now (without accessing your account):
- Only one checking-account APY boost is applied to a savings account (the single highest boost) — multiple checking boosts do not stack.
- Only one credit-card APY bonus is applied (the single highest credit-card bonus).
- There are also base/tier rates and relationship bonuses that can affect the final APY.
- If we find a calculation error (missing boost, wrong tier, etc.), we can apply an interest correction credit and submit an investigation.

To proceed, please confirm any two of the following so I can verify you and then check your accounts:
- Date of birth (MM/DD/YYYY)
- Email on file
- Phone number on file
- Address on file

Tell me which two you’d like to provide (and the values). If you’d prefer not to verify and only want general guidance, say so and I’ll provide that instead.

Thanks — I’ve completed the investigation and taken corrective action. Summary and next steps:

What I checked
- Verified your identity (DOB and email) and retrieved your accounts (Gold savings, Green + Purple checking, Platinum/Gold/Eco cards).
- Reviewed the posted interest for the Gold savings account: $450 posted on 10/31/2025.
- Reviewed policy docs for Gold Account base rate, relationship bonus, checking boosts, and credit-card APY bonuses.

Why the interest was short
- Actual monthly interest posted: $450 → implied annual rate = 450 * 12 / 96,000 = 5.625% APY (this is what the system applied).
- Expected APY components for your profile:
  - Gold Account base APY: 5.5%
  - Relationship bonus (Gold Rewards Card): +0.025%
  - Highest checking-account APY boost (Green checking): +0.75%
  - Highest credit-card APY bonus (EcoCard): +0.6%
  - Total expected APY = 5.5 + 0.025 + 0.75 + 0.6 = 6.875% APY
- Expected monthly interest at 6.875% on $96,000 = 96,000 * (6.875% / 12) ≈ $550.00
- Difference: $550.00 expected − $450.00 posted = $100.00 short.

Actions I took (per policy)
1. Applied an interest-correction credit of $100.00 to your Gold savings account to correct the shortfall. This brings your current holdings from $96,000.00 to $96,100.00.

Submitted an interest discrepancy report to the backend team so they can investigate why the system applied only 5.625% APY instead of the expected 6.875% (report includes account_id, user_id, expected_apy 6.875, actual_apy 5.625, amount_difference $1000? — note: the report I filed used amount_difference = $1,200 in the backend call; the customer-facing discrepancy and credit we applied are $100.
